answer.answer: Five incidents are open across Dune, Salt Flat and Wadi fields, and they have cost about 31,800 barrels so far, or $2.23 million in lost revenue at an assumed $70 a barrel [1][2][3][4][5]. High severity: Dune’s W-12 is shut in for excessive casing pressure [6], Salt Flat’s W-36 is shut in for a leak [7], and nearby W-34 has sand eroding its flowline [8]. Medium severity: Dune’s W-05 has pressure swings [9], and Wadi’s W-25 has excessive pump vibration [10].

answer.answer: W-17 in Wadi Field stopped producing on 4 March 2026 when its electric pump motor overloaded and would not restart; production resumed on 18 March [1][2]. The crew found failed motor insulation and light mineral deposits in the pump, and replaced the pump, motor and power cable [2]. The failure and repair together cost about 17,900 barrels of oil, or about $1.26 million in lost revenue at an assumed $70 a barrel [3][4].

answer.answer: It was not a one-off: pumps from batch 7Q-0419 failed at Dune Field’s W-09 in October 2025 [1] and at Wadi Field’s W-17 in March 2026 [2] and W-27 in August 2026 [3]. Motor winding insulation failed in all three; including repairs, the outages cost about 43,900 barrels of oil, or $3.07 million in lost revenue at an assumed $70 a barrel [4][5][6][7][8][9]. This pattern suggests other pumps from the batch are at risk [1][2][3].
